summary: We developed a biosleeve-autonomous Space health system, we realized that there is a big communication latency during missions, since the message has to be sent to mission control on earth and be analyzed, this creates a risky delay during missions and it could be critical, so we developed biosleeve that gives zero latency, it is an onboard health monitoring system that unifies physiological and behavioral tracking, detecting emergencies locally, and delivering immediate and actionable diagnostics without waiting for earth-based analysis. The importance of this project that it eliminates the communication wait during critical health events. It catches early cardiovascular, thermal, sleep, and motion anomalies before they escalate into life threatening crises, and it automates alerts and health tracking so crews stay focused on the mission rather than manual logging and guesswork.
details:
• What it does: An all-in-one monitoring device powered by an ESP32 microcontroller. It integrates a MAX30100 (pulse/SpO2), MPU6050 (motion), AHT20 (temp/humidity), and BMP280 (pressure) sensors, showing data locally on an OLED screen and remotely via a Wi-Fi web dashboard.

• Benefits: Compact, affordable, modular, and features dual local/remote access.

• Impact: Explores affordable biomedical and wearable tech applications (prototype; non-medical grade).

• Tech Stack: ESP32, C++ (Arduino IDE), HTML/CSS/JS, plus specialized sensors, OLED display, buzzer, and LiPo charging module.

• Creativity: Combines multi-domain metrics (vitals, movement, and environment) into a single, expandable, wireless system.

• Design Factors: Component compatibility, compact size, power efficiency, cost, reliability, and future scalability.
